title: Independent transcription of dossier Fig. 7 (Rob Robinette annotated Fender 5E3 schematic)

source.figure: dossier Fig. 7, image f-010-008.png, 1464x899 px (coordinates 'loc' below are approximate pixel positions in that image)
source.secondary_figure: dossier Fig. 8 (5E3 wiring layout, f-026-009.png) used only to resolve jack-switch wiring and to cross-check printed ratings
source.evidence: HISTORICAL (original 5E3 drawing; not an authenticated modern PR 728 schematic, dossier Sec. 05 and 14)
source.independence: Written before the repository netlist (data/netlist/cd57_nominal.net), docs/NETLIST.md and src/dsp/ were opened. The 'netlist_mapping' section at the end was added afterwards and is the only part that refers to the netlist.

conventions.units: ohm, farad, volt, watt; 'value' is the nominal printed number converted to SI
conventions.printed: the label exactly as it is lettered on the drawing; the drawing prints capacitors as 'uF-working_volts' without units and resistors in ohms (K = kilo, MEG = mega)
conventions.nets: every electrical node is named once in 'nets'; all ground symbols are one net GND (chassis); a wire that is drawn straight between two parts is one net
conventions.ratings: voltage/power ratings are recorded but are not electrical model parameters
conventions.jacks: a jack has a tip lug and a switch lug; with no plug inserted the switch lug is closed to the tip lug (normally-closed contact), inserting a plug opens it and puts the plug tip on the tip lug (see 'ambiguities' A1)

ambiguities.drawing: Only the Bright-Hi jack is drawn with a plug (the Fig. 7 state). A thick arrow wire runs from the Hi node (top line) down to the Lo jack's lead/bottom line, and a thin arrow wire runs from the 1 MEG's grounded end up to the top line. Neither wire has a contact symbol.
ambiguities.resolution: The thin arrow wire is the Hi jack's switch lug wired to ground; the thick arrow wire is the Lo jack's switch lug wired to the Hi node. Evidence: Fig. 8 draws exactly these two wires as lug connections (Fig. 8 'Bright Hi': ground arrow to jack 1; J1 node wired to jack 2 by an arrow), and the dossier Sec. 06 describes 34k (Hi alone), half-voltage divider with ~136k (Lo alone), which only these contacts produce. Without that reading the 1 MEG would be short-circuited by the thin wire. The normally-closed action is the standard switched-jack behaviour and is DERIVED, not drawn.
ambiguities.confidence: high for the Hi-only state (drawn), medium-high for the other three states (derived)

ambiguities.drawing: a thick black block sits on the grid wire at the top of the lower 68k
ambiguities.resolution: heavy junction mark; the lower 68k top joins the grid node (the Normal channel shows an ordinary dot at the same place)

ambiguities.drawing: the .0005 cap hangs from a thick vertical line that starts on the Bright coupling-cap output wire next to the volume wiper arrow

ambiguities.drawing: reads '25-15' on Fig. 7 (the other two 25 uF caps read '25-25'); Fig. 8 prints '25 MFD. 25 VOLTS' for the same cap
ambiguities.resolution: capacitance 25 uF is unambiguous; the working-voltage digit is recorded as 15 (as read) and flagged. It does not enter the electrical model.
ambiguities.confidence: capacitance high, voltage rating about 70 percent

ambiguities.confidence: medium-high (topology of the main load), not determinable (jack switching)
